name: pdk-pyhocon-etl
instr:
Our payments team keeps their service settings in Java `.properties` files, and our Python batch jobs now need to read them with pyhocon (in /app) next to our HOCON configs. A sample is in /data/services, and settlement.conf there shows how we include them. Today pyhocon reads a `.properties` file as if it were HOCON and gets a lot of it wrong.

`ConfigFactory.parse_file`, every form of `include` (globs too) and `pyhocon -i` should load a `.properties` file (UTF-8) with exactly the keys and values Java's `Properties.load` reads. Values stay strings and dotted keys nest like HOCON paths. When a key is both a value and the prefix of other keys, keep the nested keys and drop the value, whatever the line order. A malformed `\uXXXX` escape should raise `ConfigException`.

`include "name"` with no extension should load whichever of name.conf, name.json and name.properties exist, .conf winning over .json and .json over .properties, like the Java config library. With `required(...)` it only fails when none of them exist.

Their lists are numbered keys (`hosts.0`, `hosts.1`, ...), and `get_list` on those should return the values in index order, skipping missing numbers.

We also export settings with `pyhocon -f properties` and `HOCONConverter.to_properties`. For values without line breaks, Java has to read back exactly our keys and values, as strings, and converting that output again has to give the same file.
